## bisonR

Bayesian inference of animal social networks in R

bisonR implements the BISoN framework (Hart et al. 2023). It estimates
each edge weight from observation data as a posterior distribution (the
range of plausible values given the data and prior), so the precision of
each estimate reflects how much that dyad was sampled. These posteriors
can then be used to calculate network metrics, fit regression models and
compare networks.

[Getting started](https://bisonr.org/articles/getting_started.md)
[Function reference](https://bisonr.org/reference/index.md)

![A social network plotted with plot_network(), in which the width of
each edge shows the uncertainty in its weight.](hero-network.png)

### Edge weight models

Binary and count models of social events that account for observation
effort, with optional fixed and random effects, partial pooling and zero
inflation. Faster conjugate models, fitted without MCMC (the sampling
method that Stan uses), are available for simple cases.

[Preparing data](https://bisonr.org/articles/preparing_data.md)

### Diagnostics and plots

Trace plots of the MCMC sampler, prior and posterior predictive checks,
and network plots that show the credible interval of each edge.

[Predictive checks](https://bisonr.org/reference/plot_predictions.md)

### Downstream analyses

Posterior distributions of node and network metrics, dyadic and nodal
regression with brms, edge mixture models and non-random association
tests.

[Regression with brms](https://bisonr.org/articles/bison_brms.md)

## A first model

``` r

library(bisonR)

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)

fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "binary",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary")
)

summary(fit_edge)                                # Edge weights with credible intervals
plot_network(fit_edge, lwd = 5)                  # Sociogram showing uncertainty
extract_metric(fit_edge, "node_strength")        # Posterior of each node's strength
```

The left-hand side of the formula, `(event | effort)`, gives the number
of social events seen and how much each dyad was observed. The
right-hand side, `dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id)`, estimates an edge weight
for each dyad (pair of individuals). The [Getting
started](https://bisonr.org/articles/getting_started.md) article
explains each step.

## Installation

bisonR fits models with [Stan](https://mc-stan.org/) through the
[cmdstanr](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/) package, so install cmdstanr
and CmdStan first:

``` r

install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::check_cmdstan_toolchain(fix = TRUE)
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()
```

Then install bisonR from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("JHart96/bisonR")
```

On Windows you may need to install
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) first. The
[Windows
installation](https://bisonr.org/articles/windows_installation.md)
article covers common problems. Upcoming releases are developed on
`release/<version>` branches. To install one, use, for example,
`remotes::install_github("JHart96/bisonR@release/1.1.0")`.

## Citing bisonR

> Hart, J. D. A., Weiss, M. N., Franks, D. W., & Brent, L. J. N. (2023).
> BISoN: A Bayesian framework for inference of social networks. *Methods
> in Ecology and Evolution*, 14(9), 2411–2420.
> <https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.14171>

## Getting help

Ask questions in
[Discussions](https://github.com/JHart96/bisonR/discussions) and report
bugs in [Issues](https://github.com/JHart96/bisonR/issues).
Contributions are welcome; see the [contributing
guide](https://github.com/JHart96/bisonR/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Package index

## Fitting edge weight models

Estimate the network, with uncertainty, from observation data.

- [`bison_model()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_model.md) : Fit
  an edge weight model
- [`get_default_priors()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/get_default_priors.md)
  : Get the default priors for an edge model
- [`prior_check()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/prior_check.md) : Plot
  prior distributions
- [`prior_predictive_check()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/prior_predictive_check.md)
  : Prior predictive check

## Checking models

MCMC diagnostics, predictive checks and model comparison.

- [`plot_trace()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/plot_trace.md) : Trace
  plots of MCMC chains
- [`plot_predictions()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/plot_predictions.md)
  : Posterior predictive checks
- [`model_comparison()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/model_comparison.md)
  : Compare models with leave-one-out cross-validation

## Exploring the network

- [`summary(`*`<bison_model>`*`)`](https://bisonr.org/reference/summary.bison_model.md)
  : Summarise an edge weight model
- [`get_edgelist()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/get_edgelist.md) : Get
  the edge list with uncertainty
- [`get_effects()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/get_effects.md) : Get
  the estimates of other effects in an edge model
- [`draw_edgelist_samples()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/draw_edgelist_samples.md)
  : Draw samples of the edge list from the posterior
- [`plot_network()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/plot_network.md) :
  Plot the network with uncertainty
- [`bison_to_igraph()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_to_igraph.md)
  : Convert a fitted edge model into a list of igraph networks

## Network metrics

- [`extract_metric()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/extract_metric.md) :
  Extract posterior samples of network metrics
- [`plot_metric()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/plot_metric.md) : Plot
  the posterior distribution of a network metric

## Regression

Use network quantities in brms models while keeping their uncertainty.

- [`bison_brm()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_brm.md) : Fit a
  regression with a network metric
- [`bison_brm_get_prior()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_brm_get_prior.md)
  : List the priors of a bison_brm() regression
- [`bison_mice()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_mice.md) : Prepare
  network data for multiple imputation with the mice package

## Edge mixture models

Look for different types of social relationship.

- [`bison_mixture()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_mixture.md) :
  Fit an edge mixture model
- [`summary(`*`<bison_mixture>`*`)`](https://bisonr.org/reference/summary.bison_mixture.md)
  : Summarise an edge mixture model
- [`get_network_component_probabilities()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/get_network_component_probabilities.md)
  : Get the probability of each number of components in the network
- [`get_edge_component_probabilities()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/get_edge_component_probabilities.md)
  : Get the probability of each edge belonging to each component
- [`get_component_means()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/get_component_means.md)
  : Get the mean edge weight of each mixture component
- [`plot_mixture()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/plot_mixture.md) :
  Plot the components of an edge mixture model

## Preparing data

- [`convert_gbi_to_bison()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/convert_gbi_to_bison.md)
  : Convert a group-by-individual matrix to bisonR format
- [`convert_duration_to_binary()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/convert_duration_to_binary.md)
  : Convert duration data to binary
- [`simulate_bison_model()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/simulate_bison_model.md)
  : Simulate observation data for an edge model
- [`simulate_bison_model_mixture()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/simulate_bison_model_mixture.md)
  : Simulate observation data with several types of edge

## Saving models

- [`bison_save()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_save.md) : Save a
  fitted bisonR model to disk

- [`bison_load()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_load.md) :

  Load a bisonR model saved with
  [`bison_save()`](https://bisonr.org/reference/bison_save.md)

# Articles

### Getting started

Start here for a first analysis and the data format used by bisonR.

- [Getting started](https://bisonr.org/articles/getting_started.md):

  A first analysis: fitting an edge weight model, checking it, plotting
  the network, and using it in regressions and network metrics.

- [Preparing your data](https://bisonr.org/articles/preparing_data.md):

  The data format used by bisonR: events and observation effort,
  aggregation, directed data, unobserved dyads and group-by-individual
  matrices.

### Fitting models

Priors, diagnostics and additional effects in edge weight models.

- [Choosing and checking priors](https://bisonr.org/articles/priors.md):

  What each prior controls, the link scales, and checking priors with
  prior_check() and prior predictive checks.

- [Model diagnostics](https://bisonr.org/articles/diagnostics.md):

  MCMC diagnostics and posterior predictive checks, with a worked
  example of excess zeros.

- [Edge models with additional
  effects](https://bisonr.org/articles/edge_model_effects.md):

  Fixed effects, random effects and partial pooling in edge weight
  models, and how they change the interpretation of edge weights.

### Types of data

Worked analyses for directed networks, group-based observations and
count data.

- [Directed networks](https://bisonr.org/articles/directed_networks.md):

  Fitting, plotting and analysing directed networks, including in- and
  out-strength and dyadic regression.

- [Group-based observations](https://bisonr.org/articles/group_data.md):

  Gambit-of-the-group data: converting group-by-individual matrices,
  group-level effects and pairs that could not have been seen together.

- [Count data and continuous observation
  effort](https://bisonr.org/articles/count_data.md):

  Counts of interactions with continuous observation time, such as focal
  follows, and the interpretation of edge weights as rates.

### Analyses

Network metrics, regression, comparing networks, mixture models and
working with posterior networks.

- [Network metrics](https://bisonr.org/articles/network_metrics.md):

  Definitions of the node, edge and global metrics available in bisonR,
  and how to extract their posterior distributions.

- [Regression with brms](https://bisonr.org/articles/bison_brms.md):

  Dyadic, nodal and global regressions with bison_brm(), including
  formula syntax, scaling and priors.

- [Nodal regression](https://bisonr.org/articles/nodal_regression.md):

  A worked nodal regression relating an individual trait to centrality,
  with the metric as response or predictor.

- [Comparing
  networks](https://bisonr.org/articles/comparing_networks.md):

  Comparing two or more networks using global metrics, global
  regressions and edges present in both networks.

- [Edge mixture models](https://bisonr.org/articles/mixture_models.md):

  Looking for different types of social relationship with edge mixture
  models.

- [Working with posterior
  networks](https://bisonr.org/articles/posterior_networks.md):

  Using posterior draws directly: igraph networks, metrics not provided
  by bisonR, community detection, edge contrasts and saving models.

### Help

- [Installing cmdstanr on
  Windows](https://bisonr.org/articles/windows_installation.md):

  Solutions to common problems when installing cmdstanr and CmdStan on
  Windows.
